attribution: None of these have a brewing datasheet, so every PPG here is derived from the product's own Nutrition Facts panel via lib/fermentable-math.ts: PPG = 46 x (total carbohydrate - fibre) / serving weight. Panels change between reformulations and countries — check the box you actually bought. Values are potential extract; starch-based items still need enzymatic conversion.

fermentables.name: Fruity Pebbles
fermentables.description: Rice-based cereal that is nearly all sugar and gelatinised rice starch — hence a very high potential extract for a cereal. A pastry-sour and milkshake-IPA favourite.
fermentables.flavorNotes: Artificial fruit punch, sweet cereal milk.
fermentables.usageNotes: The rice starch is already gelatinised (it was extruded), so it converts readily in a normal mash — but it still needs diastatic malt. The colour is mostly water-soluble dye that mostly washes out. Expect sticky, dusty handling.

fermentables.name: Cocoa Pebbles
fermentables.description: The cocoa version — same rice base, with cocoa for a light chocolate-cereal note.

fermentables.name: Cap'n Crunch
fermentables.description: Corn-and-oat cereal with a distinct toasted-sweet character that survives fermentation better than most.
fermentables.flavorNotes: Toasted corn, brown sugar, cereal milk.

fermentables.name: Cinnamon Toast Crunch
fermentables.description: Wheat-and-rice cereal carrying real cinnamon sugar — one of the few novelty cereals whose flavour genuinely carries through.
fermentables.usageNotes: Contains added fat from the coating; keep the percentage moderate or head retention suffers.

fermentables.name: Lucky Charms
fermentables.description: Oat cereal plus marshmallows. The marshmallow portion is nearly pure fermentable sugar and gelatin.

fermentables.name: Froot Loops
fermentables.description: Corn, wheat, and oat blend with citrus-forward artificial fruit flavour.

fermentables.name: Corn Flakes
fermentables.description: Plain corn flakes are effectively pre-gelatinised flaked maize with a little sugar and salt — a genuinely serviceable corn adjunct, not just a novelty.
fermentables.usageNotes: Choose unsweetened; the salt content is negligible at normal rates.

fermentables.name: Rice Krispies
fermentables.description: Puffed rice — already gelatinised, so it converts without a cereal mash. One of the highest-extract cereal adjuncts.
fermentables.usageNotes: A practical shortcut when you want rice character without cooking raw rice.

fermentables.name: Frosted Flakes
fermentables.description: Sugar-coated corn flakes; the coating is directly fermentable, the flake needs conversion.

fermentables.name: Cheerios
fermentables.description: Whole-oat cereal — high fibre drags the extract down, but it brings oat-like body and a toasty note.

fermentables.name: Graham Crackers
fermentables.description: Honey-graham flour biscuit; the go-to for s'mores stouts and pastry beers.
fermentables.usageNotes: Contains fat — moderate the percentage to protect foam.

fermentables.name: Marshmallows
fermentables.description: Corn syrup, sugar, and gelatin. Fully fermentable, so it adds alcohol rather than the sweetness people expect.
fermentables.usageNotes: For actual marshmallow sweetness use lactose or vanilla instead — the sugar here ferments out completely. Gelatin means not vegan, and it will foam violently in the boil.

fermentables.name: Sandwich Cookies (Oreo-style)
fermentables.description: Cocoa biscuit with a fat-based creme filling.
fermentables.usageNotes: Roughly 20% fat by weight — this is a foam killer. Cocoa nibs plus lactose give the same idea without wrecking head retention.

fermentables.name: Hard Candy (Jolly Rancher-style)
fermentables.description: Essentially flavoured, coloured sucrose and corn syrup — ferments out completely, leaving only the flavouring.

fermentables.name: Cotton Candy
fermentables.description: Spun sucrose — chemically identical to table sugar at 46 PPG. Only the flavouring and dye survive fermentation.

fermentables.name: Gummy Candy
fermentables.description: Glucose syrup, sucrose, and gelatin. Ferments dry; the gelatin can actually help clarity as a fining.

fermentables.name: Peanut Butter
fermentables.description: Almost no fermentable sugar and about 50% fat.
fermentables.usageNotes: Strongly discouraged as a direct addition — the fat destroys head retention and can turn rancid. Use powdered/defatted peanut flour (PB2-style) or natural flavouring instead.

fermentables.name: Sweet Potato
fermentables.description: Starchy root with an earthy sweetness; roast before mashing for real flavour. The base of Japanese imo-shochu.

fermentables.name: Potato
fermentables.description: Mostly water and starch. Little flavour contribution, but a traditional vodka and poitín base.
fermentables.usageNotes: Must be cooked to gelatinise, then converted with malt or enzymes.

fermentables.name: Cacao Nibs
fermentables.description: Flavouring, not a fermentable — contributes essentially no gravity. The clean way to get chocolate without cookie fat.
fermentables.usageNotes: Typical: 2–4 oz per 5 gal in secondary, optionally soaked in neutral spirit.

fermentables.name: Vanilla Bean
fermentables.description: Pure flavouring with no fermentable content; the honest way to add the sweetness people wrongly expect from marshmallows.
fermentables.usageNotes: 1–3 beans per 5 gal, split and soaked in vodka, added at packaging.

fermentables.name: Coffee
fermentables.description: No fermentable sugar. Cold-brew added at packaging keeps the aroma and avoids the harsh tannins hot extraction pulls.
